No, helium does not form covalent bonds. Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electrons between atoms in order to achieve an equal number of valence electrons on each atom. Helium is a noble gas and its electron configuration is \(1s^2\). Since helium has one electron in its outer shell and it doesn't have enough electrons to satisfy the octet rule (which requires that each element have 8 electrons), it cannot form any covalent bonds with other atoms.

In fact, helium exhibits a very stable state as an inert gas.
